title: Cross-SDK invocation bridge and ergonomic wrappers for function-calling (schema safety, streaming resume, retries)
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description:
Problem statement: customers building function/tool-calling workflows are experiencing mismatches between declared function schemas and runtime arguments, awkward streaming ergonomics for long-running tool outputs, and unclear retry semantics when partial streamed responses have been emitted. Goal: ship a cross-SDK (Python/TypeScript/Go) invocation helper library that enforces schema validation at call-site, provides ergonomic synchronous + async streaming patterns with resume tokens, and codifies safe retry/idempotency semantics for both non-streaming and streaming invocations.

Proposed approach: implement a small, language-idiomatic layer per SDK that: 1) accepts a machine-readable function schema (JSON Schema + optional typed typedefs) and validates the call payload before sending; 2) surfaces typed response coercion and runtime guards; 3) provides a StreamingInvocation abstraction that yields partial chunks and exposes a resume token so callers can checkpoint and resume after network hiccups; 4) introduces an invocation metadata envelope carrying idempotency_key, client_request_id, and causal_trace headers for safe retries; 5) offers default retry policies (transparent retry for pre-call failures, conservative for streaming resumptions) and hooks for customers to override.

Language specifics: Python will provide sync/async flavors with dataclass-backed schema adapters and mypy-friendly stubs; TypeScript will generate typed function definitions (with overloads for streaming vs non-streaming) and integrate with existing SDK promise/stream APIs; Go will expose a small interface package with context-based cancellation, backoff pluggability, and a compact checkpoint token format for resume.

Non-goals: auto-generating server-side function dispatchers, replacing third-party schema validators across the board, or changing the API surface of Redwood's core call endpoints.
acceptance_criteria:
- Validator accepts JSON Schema and rejects calls with schema mismatch (unit tests covering optional/required/enum/array cases).
- Examples in Python/TS/Go show idiomatic usage for normal calls and streaming calls with resume tokens.
- Retry semantics documented and exercised: pre-send transient failures retried automatically, streaming resumes validated against resume token and retried without duplicating already-emitted chunks.
- Types/stubs published to package registries (PyPI/@types or bundled .d.ts) and minimal build pipelines added.
- Security review completed for invocation envelope (idempotency header usage) and no sensitive info is persisted in resume tokens.
- Integration e2e tests against a local harness with injected network failures pass.
notes:
Trade-offs discussed on design doc: keep resume token minimal (opaque base64) to avoid leaking internal state vs. richer semantic checkpoints that are easier for debugging. We chose opaque token with server-side mapping + short TTL.

Telemetry: add metrics for validate_failures, resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, and average_resume_latency. Instrumentation to be low-cardinality.

Backward compatibility: default helpers are opt-in; older SDK call signatures remain supported while we iterate on ergonomics. Migration doc to be authored for customers.

Open questions: should resume tokens be client-verifiable (HMAC) to avoid server-side state? (security asked for HMAC option behind feature flag).
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete for Python adapter; prototype library validates schema via jsonschema and produces dataclass wrappers. Local tests for required/optional fields passing. (artifact: docs/priv/spikes/sdk-func-schema-proto.md)

2026-03-03: TypeScript sketch done - used io-ts fallback for runtime validation in prototype; streaming API surface explored with readable-stream events. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412
2026-03-04: Design review with Security & API - agreed on opaque resume token + optional HMAC feature flag. Security requested gated rollout and rotation plan for HMAC keys.

2026-03-05: Go interface prototype implemented; checkpoint token format finalized (opaque base64 of server nonce plus short TTL). Added initial unit tests for resume path. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/427
review_comments: PM (Lena R.) - Please ensure examples include a typical canary flow for Dedicated customers and show how to pin model variants when resuming.
Design (Maya C.) - API ergonomics look good for Python/TS but Go surface needs clearer naming for Resume/Checkpoint to match go-idioms.
Security (Anand S.) - Approve opaque token approach but require HMAC option; add key-rotation doc and retention limits for tokens.
Infra (Kai L.) - Need a migration plan for server-side resume mapping to avoid state blow-up under high-traffic tenants; propose TTL + LRU eviction + telemetry to monitor mapping size.
tests_and_qa:
Unit tests: validator edge cases, schema mismatch errors, streaming chunk dedup and resume.
Integration tests: harness with a toy function endpoint that emits 100 chunks; inject TCP drop at chunk 47 and assert resume picks up at 48.
Load testing: ensure resume mapping behaves under 10k concurrent checkpoints (simulate in staging).
implementation_plan: 1) Stabilize validation lib and publish language idioms (week 1). 2) Implement streaming invocation abstraction + checkpointing in each SDK (week 2). 3) Add retry policies and idempotency headers, run e2e tests (week 3). 4) Security review and feature-flag rollout to limited customers, docs + migration guides (week 4).
docs_and_examples: Python example: from redwood_sdk import invoke_function, SchemaAdapter; schema = {...}; ret = invoke_function('calc-sum', payload, schema_adapter=schema);
TypeScript example: import { callFunction } from '@redwood/sdk'; const res = await callFunction('translate', args, { validate: true });
Go example: client.Invoke(ctx, name, args, sdk.WithResumeHandler(func(token string) { /* checkpoint */ } ))
